submitted.rationale: Index 0 (Fe0.84Sb0.16) had the highest measured EQE, 0.212%. EQE rose steadily with Fe content: about 0 at index 12, 0.151% at index 4 and 0.212% at index 0. This fits a hematite-rich, Sb-modified photoanode that absorbs 2.4 eV light, and MACE puts hematite on the convex hull.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE was about -0.008%, effectively zero. XRD looks like single-phase rutile FeSbO4, which is inactive despite a predicted 2.08 eV gap.
Measured 0.151%, lower than index 0. XRD shows mixed phases.
Not measured. The predicted gap is small (1.28 eV), and EQE was falling toward the Sb-rich side.

consultations.verdict: Support: MEGNet HSE gap for rutile FeSbO4 is 2.08 eV, below the 2.4 eV photon energy, so it can absorb. The XRD at index 12 looks single-phase rutile. FeSb2O6 (1.28 eV) is less likely to be a good photoanode, and hematite (2.77 eV predicted) is marginal.

Support: MACE puts hematite Fe2O3 on the hull, so a stable hematite-like phase should form on the Fe-rich side. Hematite is a known photoanode that absorbs 2.4 eV light. The XRD at index 4 shows extra, non-rutile peaks, which suggests an Fe-oxide phase next to FeSbO4. The rutile FeSbO4 at index 12 gave about 0 EQE, so I am moving toward the Fe-rich end.

Partial support. MEGNet predicts a 0.18 eV, near-metallic gap for the Fe3O4 spinel, which would hurt photoactivity if spinel forms. On the other hand, EQE went up as Fe increased (index 12: about 0; index 4: 0.15), and hematite was stable in MACE. The most Fe-rich sample, index 0, should have the most hematite, so I will spend the last measurement there.
